stemMd: A council favors replacing street lamps with efficient models, predicting lower electricity use. Which evidence most directly threatens the prediction?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The new lamps have a longer expected life.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The lamps are supplied by a local firm.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The installation requires temporary road closures.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The replacement plan also greatly increases the number of lamps and their nightly operating hours.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Residents prefer the new color of light.

explanationMd: Efficiency per lamp or per hour is different from total consumption. More lamps operating longer could outweigh lower power use per lamp. The prediction must compare the complete operating systems.

distractorRationale.e: Preference does not quantify total consumption.
distractorRationale.c: Temporary closures do not determine ongoing electricity demand.
distractorRationale.a: Longevity does not itself offset lower power consumption.
distractorRationale.b: Supplier location does not establish electricity use.
